chunks: Abul Abbas Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Taleqani (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Abu Sa’id al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Ado’we quoted Muhammad ibn Khalilan ibn Ali al-Ab’basi, on the authority of Abi Khalilan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of his forefathers that Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said:
We are distinguished by five things: eloquence in speech, beauty, generosity, nobility, and favor with women.
ai.seo_question: What are the five special virtues attributed to Ali ibn Abi Talib in this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ali (as) highlights five distinctive traits—eloquence, beauty, generosity, bravery, and charm with women—that characterize the Ahl al-Bayt. These virtues reflect both their spiritual nobility and their social leadership, demonstrating how divine favor manifests in both inner character and outward presence. This enumeration underscores the comprehensive excellence of the Imams, encompassing intellectual, physical, and social dimensions.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-41 Abul Abbas Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Taleqani - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abu Sa’id al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Ado’we quoted Muhammad ibn Khalilan ibn Ali al-Ab’basi, on the authority of Abi Khalilan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of his forefathers that Ali ibn Abi Talib (MGB) said, “
Five things are especially ours: eloquence in speech, beautifulness, generosity, nobility and benefiting from women.”
